a number of novel N‐sulphonyl and N‐N‐sulphonylamino noscapine derivatives were prepared and evaluated as anticancer agents, with the most potent derivative displaying sub‐micromole anticancer activity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis and evaluation of a novel series of N‐substituted noscapine derivatives, and we have identified a number of compounds that are potent and selective antiproliferatives.
the development of novel noscapinoids as a potential treatment option for cancer.
the development of a novel class of noscapine derivatives that display improved anticancer activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the replacement of the 6′N‐methyl group with a range of sulfonyl‐substituents, particularly the 6′(1‐methylimidazolyl)sulfonylnoscapine derivative (14 q), results in enhanced anticancer efficacy.
N‐substituted noscapine derivatives are a promising novel class of anticancer agents.
the N‐sulfonamoyl derivatives 14 b, 14 c, 14 e and 14 q, and the N‐sulfinyl derivative 14 f, are the best candidates in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N‐sulfo‐ and N‐sulfa‐noscapine derivatives represent an important class of noscapinoids with potential anticancer properties.
N‐substituents of noscapine can be modified to enhance anticancer activity and that N‐substitution with a sulfamoyl group can lead to a novel class of noscapinoids with potent cytotoxic activities.
the introduction of a 6‐N‐sulfonylated noscapine analogue with a bulky substituent at the C‐4 position is an effective strategy to generate potent noscapinoids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N‐sulfo group is a promising pharmacophore that could be used to generate more potent and selective noscapinoids for anticancer drug discovery.
N‐sulfinyl noscapine analogs are promising anticancer agents with potential for further development.
N‐sulphonylated noscapinoids are a novel class of anticancer agents with promising activity against a range of tumour cell lines.
